context_requirements: Expression of the drug's direct target(s) in the assayed cell line (e.g., PTGS1/PTGS2, PPARG/PPARD, FFAR1, TRPV1, SLC8A1, ACSL3/4, FADS1).
An intact downstream signaling or metabolic pathway that can be modulated by the target (e.g., prostaglandin synthesis, PPAR transcriptional activity, fatty-acid handling).
For transcriptional readout, the affected pathway must feed into gene-expression changes within 6–24 h; purely platelet-restricted mechanisms will not respond in these non-platelet cell lines.
falsifiers: No consistent transcriptional response across any of the nine cell lines at 6 h or 24 h.
Changes that are indistinguishable from vehicle or from generic stress responses without any target-linked gene signature.
A response pattern that is equally strong in cell lines lacking the relevant targets (e.g., PTGS1/PTGS2, PPARG/PPARD, FFAR1, TRPV1, SLC8A1, ACSL3/4, FADS1).
Proximal changes that occur only at 24 h with no early (6 h) component, contradicting a direct mechanism.
A signature dominated by generic proliferation or cell-cycle arrest with no specific target-pathway genes.
